caption: Newanforbi v. Candelaria, et al.
claims: Writ of Administrative Mandate (CCP §§1094.5, 473(d); Veh. Code §13559) — Set aside void APS Decision
status: NOT PURSUING — fee-payment deadline (~Jul. 27, 2026) lapsed by deliberate choice after the Santa Clara transfer made Sacramento litigation impractical. Underlying CDL-suspension theory remains live in Matter 7. PDFs under Matter 33/from-08/.
note: Fee deadline lapsed ~Jul. 27, 2026 — not pursued further; Matter 7 remains the live vehicle for the same underlying theory. PDF set relocated to Matter 33 on August 7, 2026.
defendants: Diana Candelaria, Driver Safety Hearing Officer, California DMV (official capacity); California Department of Motor Vehicles; Does 1-10
causes: Count I — Want of Statutory Predicate: No 'Lawful Arrest' (Veh. Code §13353(a)(1); CCP §1094.5(b)) — APS refusal suspension lacks 'lawful arrest' predicate; PC §849(b)(1) Detention Certificate (Nov. 5, 2024) irrevocably destroyed that predicate before the Jan. 24, 2025 hearing

Count II — Failure to Proceed in the Manner Required by Law (CCP §1094.5(b); Topanga Ass'n v. County of L.A., 11 Cal.3d 506) — Decision does not mention Detention Certificate; dismisses arguments as 'unpersuasive' without analysis; mischaracterizes record; never applies Mercer v. DMV or People v. Sanders

Count III — Findings Unsupported by the Weight of the Evidence (CCP §1094.5(c); Berlinghieri v. DMV, 33 Cal.3d 392) — Dashcam audio directly contradicts DS-367's 'strong distinct odor of alcohol'; only liquid identified on scene was urine; no objective signs of impairment on video; walk-and-turn abandoned by officers; no pass/fail FST standard

Count IV — Structural Bias — Unconstitutional Dual-Role Framework (U.S. Const. 14th Amend.; Cal. Const. art. I §7) — DMV hearing officer serves as both advocate and adjudicator; structural error under Knudsen v. DMV (no showing of actual prejudice required); framework condemned in Cal. DUI Lawyers Ass'n v. DMV, Knudsen, Clarke v. Gordon

Count V — Excess of Jurisdiction — Adjudication of a Non-Existent Subject Matter (CCP §1094.5(b)) — Decision void; rendered in clear absence of jurisdiction over subject matter that did not legally exist at time of hearing
key_facts: Verified Petition for Writ of Administrative Mandate challenging DMV APS Decision (Feb. 11, 2025, APS Case No. 34739340) suspending Class A CDL (License F7953179) for one year (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026). Central dispositive fact: Dublin CHP issued PC §849(b)(1) Detention Certificate (CHP Case No. RJ68845, Nov. 5, 2024) more than two months before the Jan. 24, 2025 APS hearing, certifying the Nov. 1, 2024 stop was 'a detention only, not an arrest.' APS jurisdiction under Veh. Code §13353(a)(1) is conditioned on a 'lawful arrest' — a predicate irrevocably destroyed by CHP's own agency-issued certificate before the hearing ever occurred. Respondent Candelaria's four-page Decision never once mentions the Detention Certificate and dismisses all petitioner's arguments as 'unpersuasive' without analysis. Dashcam transcript (00:54:36 – 01:57:10) shows: (1) liquid identified as urine, not alcohol, at 00:58:51 by Officer Melano ('This is piss'); (2) Officer Meza-Gonzalez declines to smell the cup; (3) no officer contemporaneously verbalizes alcohol odor in 62 minutes of recording; (4) walk-and-turn abandoned due to 'uneven ground'; (5) officers acknowledge no pass/fail FST standard (01:09:52); (6) PAS test expressly optional (01:10:54); (7) arrest ordered one second after lawful PAS refusal. DS-367 sworn claim of 'strong distinct odor of an alcoholic beverage' directly contradicted by dashcam. No accusatory pleading filed by Alameda County DA. Petitioner submitted five-page Personal Statement (Dec. 9, 2024) citing Terry v. Ohio, Mercer v. DMV, People v. Sanders, PC §§849(b)(1), 849(c), 849.5, 851.6(a). CDL suspension caused loss of commercial driving employment; CDL loss cited as aggravating factor in Nov. 2025 Discharge Review (Matter 9). Monetary consequential damages reserved for federal action (2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK).
procedural_status: Verified Petition for Writ of Administrative Mandate filed May 18, 2026 (26WM000135) challenging Candelaria's Feb. 11, 2025 APS decision as void ab initio. Fee waiver denied May 19 for incomplete income information; hearing July 17, 2026 — Petitioner did not appear after the June 29 retaliatory transfer to Santa Clara (Matter 30). Non-appearance triggered a ~Jul. 27 fee-payment deadline that lapsed without payment or a revised FW-001 by deliberate choice. Equitable/vacatur track abandoned; Matter 7 remains the primary damages vehicle. Dated beats live in timeline.json.
damages: Equitable: (a) set aside Decision in its entirety; (b) vacate one-year Class A CDL suspension (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026); (c) restore commercial driving privileges nunc pro tunc to Feb. 20, 2025; (d) vacate $125 reissue fee (Veh. Code §§14904, 14906); (e) vacate three-year SR-22 financial-responsibility requirement (Veh. Code §16430); (f) expunge all suspension notations from driving record; (g) refund $125 reissue fee with interest from date of payment. SR-22 insurance: Policy No. GPCP-00713747-00; $403.04 paid to date; $29.55/month; 3-year exposure ≥$1,340.04 (consequential damages reserved for federal action, 2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK). Attorney's fees under CCP §1021.5.
risk: Favorable: Candelaria sued in official capacity only — no individual capacity immunity arguments. Detention Certificate is categorically dispositive: CHP's own agency issued PC §849(b)(1) certificate reclassifying event as 'detention only, not an arrest' more than two months before the Jan. 24, 2025 hearing. Under Knudsen structural error doctrine, no showing of actual prejudice is required. Decision's failure to mention Detention Certificate anywhere is the central due process violation. APS decision is void (not merely voidable) for want of subject-matter jurisdiction, which cannot be insulated by the 34-day limitations period of Veh. Code §13559(a). Independent judgment standard (Berlinghieri/Daniels) applies because CDL is a fundamental vested right and means of livelihood.
